limitations: Cloud timings vary substantially, including fallback controls whose allocations and work are effectively unchanged. Retain all measurements; do not interpret apparent fallback speedups or regressions as reliable effects. RSS is process lifetime peak via Linux wait4, includes input creation, warmup and allocator retention; separate counting-allocator probes measure requested Rust heap bytes, not allocator metadata. DefaultHasher fingerprints compare only binaries built with this same Rust version. Linux wait4 ru_maxrss also retains a pre-exec parent-memory floor: small-process values can therefore overstate the executed Rust process peak. The Python measurement parent stayed small; large 135–290 MiB cases are above that floor, but these remain lifetime rather than matching-only RSS figures. Historical numbers are preserved. The committed harness additionally reports its own post-exec Linux VmHWM for future runs; that field was not collected in these historical measurements.

initial.methodology: Release builds, 3 fresh processes per variant, 1 untimed warmup + 5 timed matching calls per process. Input construction and process startup excluded. Global allocator profiling disabled for timings. Peak RSS from Linux wait4 ru_maxrss covers whole fresh process. Before and after source differ only by match_tables borrowing branch. Alternated order across fresh processes; exact ordered pair/score-bit/details hash equality required.
